chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Saeed ibn Janaah, from Abu Khalid al-Zaydi, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A group of people came to al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and said, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! We see in your dwelling things we dislike.' And in his house were rugs and cushions. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'We marry women, so we give them their dowries, and they buy whatever they wish. There is nothing for us from it.'

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Husayn have luxury items in his house if he was known for piety?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) clarifies that the furnishings in his home were acquired through the dowries (*mahr*) given to his wives, which became their exclusive property to spend as they pleased. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that a wife’s dowry is separate from her husband’s wealth, countering critics who viewed such domestic comforts as impropriety or extravagance. The incident underscores the practical application of marital financial rights within the Ahl al-Bayt's household.
